newsitem.title: IRAQ: Five injured in Baghdad explosion, group says.
newsitem.headline: Five injured in Baghdad explosion, group says.

text.p: An explosion rocked the Iraqi capital Baghdad on Tuesday, injuring five people and wrecking a hospital laboratory, the Iraq-based Iranian opposition group Mujahideen Khalq said.
"At least five people have been injured and one of them had his leg amputated and Baghdad's central laboratory has been wrecked and another hospital partly damaged," a Mujahideen source told Reuters.

The source said the explosion, which was heard in many parts of the Iraqi capital, resulted from the firing of a 125-kg shell from what he described as "a super mortar gun" orginally directed at the Mujahideen headquarters in Baghdad.
He said the mortar created a crater five metres (15 feet) in diameter and three metres (10 feet) deep. He said it fell 500 metres (yards) away from their main office in Baghdad.
"Three such mortars were fired against our headquarters from a distance of 600 metres (yards) but only one of them exploded," he said.
He said the attackers had timed their mortar guns and hid them in a lorry about 700 metres (yards) away from the Mujahideen office in the heart of the Iraqi capital.
